subject: Re: Order Form - sole remedy, credit cap and liability carve-outs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <j.blake@acme.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Lang <p.lang@acme.io>, contracts@acme.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form: liability cap + SLA credits

Vanessa —

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Our legal team reviewed the MSA redlines and flagged two items that are blockers for Acme sign-off:

1) Liability cap: the current language that caps liability at the "fees paid in the prior 12 months" is too low given our potential exposure. We need either a higher multiple (e.g., 2x ARR) or a flat-dollar minimum.

2) SLA / sole remedy: the proposed sole remedy language appears to make service credits the exclusive remedy for SLA failures. We need clarification that credits do not extinguish other remedies for willful misconduct, IP infringement, or breaches of confidentiality. Also, we're concerned about a hard cap that prevents meaningful recovery for systemic outages.

Attached is a redline from our counsel with suggested edits. Can we set up a quick call with your legal team to resolve these points this week? Procurement needs a path to finalize the PO.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Corp

Attachments: Acme_MSA_comments_20260630.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <j.blake@acme.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: liability cap + SLA credits

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick review and the redline. We're close on this, and happy to jump on a call. High level responses below so you have context ahead of any legal call:

- Liability cap: our standard position for Order Forms tied to hosted inference is a cap equal to aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months. That is our default to balance commercial predictability and unlimited tail risk. We can offer a limited carve-out approach: (a) carve-outs for gross negligence/willful misconduct, IP indemnity, and breaches of confidentiality (those remain uncapped), and (b) offer a one-time uplift to the cap for enterprise deals when negotiated as a commercial concession (we typically move to 1.5x or 2x annual committed spend with exec approval).

- SLA / sole remedy: our standard SLA language makes service credits the sole and exclusive contractual remedy for specified SLA failures. We explicitly exclude that sole remedy limitation from applying to liability carved-outs (IP, gross negligence, willful misconduct, data breaches). In practice that means credits are the remedy for availability/performance shortfalls but do not limit recovery for catastrophic conduct.

- Credit caps: for Order Forms we typically cap monthly credits at 50% of the monthly service fee and annual aggregate credits at 100% of annual fees for the affected service. We can discuss tightening these numbers if needed.

I've attached the redlined MSA and a suggested Order Form language that (I believe) addresses both parties' concerns. Can you confirm availability for a 30-min legal alignment tomorrow (10–12 PT)? If your counsel prefers, we can have our GC or head of legal join.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v2_redline.docx, OrderForm_ACME_v3.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: liability cap + SLA credits

Team —

Quick internal note on negotiating posture for legal:

- Keep the standard MSA cap (12-month fees) as the baseline. If Acme insists on higher, authorize commercial to offer up to 1.5x for up to $250k uplift; any request beyond that needs approvals (sales leadership + finance).

- Make explicit the carve-outs: IP indemnity, bodily injury/personal injury (if relevant), gross negligence/willful misconduct, and data privacy breaches. These should be uncapped.

- SLA credits: proposed compromise in the attached spreadsheet (SLA_Credits_Table.xlsx) — monthly per-service cap at 40–50% of monthly fee; incident cap at 25% per incident; annual aggregate capped at 100% of yearly fees.

- Sole remedy clause: allow the clause to stand for availability/performance only; add a parenthetical that it does not apply to the carve-outs. That language keeps our commercial protections while addressing Acme's counsel's IP/confidentiality concerns.

If Acme asks for language that nullifies the cap for systemic outages, we should require a narrowly defined "catastrophic outage" trigger and quantify remedies (credits plus potential short-term fee reprieve) — not open-ended liability.

Karthik
VP, Sales Operations (redwood_internal note)

From: Acme Corp Legal <contracts@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <j.blake@acme.io>, Peter Lang <p.lang@acme.io>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: liability cap + SLA credits

Vanessa, Karthik —

Thanks for the summary. Counsel's position is that: (1) the cap tied to prior 12 months' fees is acceptable only if we get a minimum floor (we proposed $500k) and (2) the sole remedy language needs to expressly preserve other remedies for systemic outages caused by operator error or prolonged downtime exceeding 24 hours.

Suggested redline excerpt: "Service credits shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for Service Unavailability as defined in Section X, provided that this limitation shall not apply to (a) claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) claims for infringement of Customer's intellectual property, (c) breaches of Customer Data confidentiality, or (d) systemic outages that persist for more than 24 continuous hours and which are not resolved through reasonable remedial actions."

We understand you prefer an aggregate cap; the floor and the systemic-outage carve-out are non-negotiable for Acme. Are you able to confirm whether Redwood can accept a $500k floor (as a one-time concession tied to this Order Form)?

Regards,
Alyssa Chen
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp

Attachment: Acme_MSA_counter_redline_20260701.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <contracts@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <j.blake@acme.io>, p.lang@acme.io
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: liability cap + SLA credits

Alyssa —

Thanks — this is helpful and very clear. Internal next steps on our side: I'll escalate the $500k floor request to Sales Leadership and Finance to evaluate commercial impact; Karthik, can you run the numbers on potential exposure and margin impact if we accept a $500k floor for AC-2026-045? I'd like an answer by EOD tomorrow so we can avoid delaying procurement.

Operationally, we can accept the systemic-outage carve-out if we narrow the trigger: propose "systemic outage" be defined as (i) an unplanned interruption impacting >= 90% of customer tokens processed for the service AND (ii) continuous duration > 24 hours. The remedy for that narrowly defined event would be credits up to 200% of the monthly fee for the affected service (not unlimited liability). This gives Acme stronger protection while keeping our commercial exposure bounded.

If you agree, we'll generate a clean redline incorporating: (a) explicit carve-outs (IP, gross negligence, confidentiality), (b) floor discussion for the cap (pending approvals), and (c) the narrow systemic-outage definition + 200% monthly credit remedy.

I'll coordinate an alignment call with Alyssa / Jordan / Karthik and our legal lead tomorrow afternoon. Thanks everyone for the constructive back-and-forth.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
